Education Domain - Academic Records Management

Academic records management is strictly regulated by FERPA and institutional record retention policies.

For Transcript Request: Required attributes include student identifier (name and student ID or SSN), date of birth for verification, request date, delivery method (electronic or physical), recipient institution/organization name and address, and payment for transcript fee if applicable. Signature authorization required.

For Certificate Verification: Required attributes include certificate number or student identifier, certificate type (degree, diploma, etc.), issuing institution, and verification requester information. Third-party verification requests require student authorization or legal basis (employment, licensing).

For Grade Report: Required attributes include student identifier, academic term, courses enrolled, grades earned, GPA, and credit hours. Grade reports are part of official education records protected by FERPA. Access restricted to student (if 18+) or parents (if minor).

For Transfer Certificate: Required attributes include student name, date of birth, student identifier, dates of enrollment, academic standing, fee clearance status, conduct record, and reason for transfer. Issuing institution details and receiving institution name (if known).

For Migration Certificate: Required attributes include student name, date of birth, previous institution details, new institution details, migration reason, academic records summary, and fee payment. Required for inter-state or inter-country transfers.

UNNECESSARY Attributes: Religion, ethnicity, caste are unnecessary for academic records unless part of institutional demographic reporting (aggregated, anonymized). Political affiliation is never required. Medical information is unnecessary unless relevant to academic accommodations.

FERPA prohibits disclosure of education records without consent, except to school officials with legitimate educational interest, in response to subpoenas, or for health/safety emergencies.

Record Retention: Educational institutions must retain academic records per state requirements (typically permanent for transcripts, 5-7 years for supporting documents).

Data Minimization: Academic records should contain only information necessary for educational purposes and legal compliance.
